sourceType: Verified partial practice based on a marked 2024 Assessment 2 review. Only clearly visible, independently sensible items are included.
sourceLimitations: The public review exposes only part of the 25-question quiz. Ambiguous or textbook-specific items that could not be independently confirmed are withheld.

questions.text: Have many large organisations created internal websites or platforms that support online social networking among employees?
questions.explanation:
Enterprise social platforms and internal collaboration sites can support employee communication, communities and knowledge sharing inside an organisation.

Student note: Internal social networking is about employee collaboration, not only public social media.

questions.text: A privacy policy where information is not used for an additional purpose unless the customer actively agrees is called:
questions.explanation:
Opt-in requires a positive choice before the additional use is allowed. Opt-out assumes the use unless the person objects.

Student note: Opt-in = permission first.

questions.text: A banner advertisement loading on a web page counts as an advertising:
questions.explanation:
An impression records that an advert was displayed/served. A click requires the user to interact with it.

Student note: Impression = seen/served; click = interacted.

questions.text: In an online auction, which information can help a cautious bidder judge whether a seller has behaved reliably in previous transactions?
questions.explanation:
Past seller ratings, feedback and transaction records can help a bidder judge reputation and risk.

Student note: Reputation information reduces uncertainty; it does not guarantee a future transaction.

questions.text: Advertising directed to a known recipient through channels such as mail, telephone or email is called:
questions.explanation:
Addressable media targets identifiable recipients rather than broadcasting the same message to an unknown mass audience.

Student note: The key word is identifiable/addressable recipient.

questions.text: Rational branding depends mainly on a broad emotional appeal.
questions.explanation:
Rational branding focuses on concrete benefits, features or reasons. Emotional branding is the approach centred more strongly on feelings and identity.

Student note: Rational = reasons/benefits; emotional = feelings/identity.

questions.text: An intelligent shopping agent that learns a customer's preferences and recommends products is commonly described as a:
questions.explanation:
A personal-shopper agent uses preference information to help filter choices and make recommendations.

Student note: The important feature is personalised recommendation, not simply listing products.

questions.text: In behaviour-based categories of website visitors, people whose main goal is to stay in touch through chat, forums and social networking are called:
questions.explanation:
The connector category describes visitors focused on communicating and maintaining social contact online.

Student note: Learn what the category does, not only the label.

questions.text: Email sent to people who explicitly requested information about a topic or product is called:
questions.explanation:
Opt-in email is sent after the recipient has actively requested or agreed to receive that type of communication.

Student note: Consent is what separates opt-in messaging from unsolicited spam.

questions.text: A hidden identifying code embedded into a digital image or audio file is a digital:
questions.explanation:
A digital watermark embeds identifying or ownership-related information into digital media, often in a way that is difficult to notice visually or audibly.

Student note: Watermarking is about identifying media; encryption is about making content unreadable without a key.

questions.text: A symbol adopted with the intention of authenticating a writing is a:
questions.explanation:
A signature is used to authenticate or indicate approval of a writing; electronic-signature law can recognise digital forms when requirements are met.

Student note: The legal idea is intent to authenticate, not whether ink is used.

questions.text: Online distribution can still cause sales losses or cannibalisation for publishers.
questions.explanation:
Digital distribution can create new revenue but can also replace sales from another channel, enable unauthorised copying or change pricing pressure.

Student note: A new channel can add sales and also shift sales away from an old channel.

questions.text: A seller that builds a brand and then sells through printed information mailed to customers who order by mail or telephone is using the:
questions.explanation:
The catalog model uses a product catalog to present offerings and lets customers place orders through supported channels.

Student note: The defining feature is selling from a catalog, not whether the catalog is digital or printed.
